title: Falcon 9 NROL-136 (SLC-4E)

azimuth_deg.derived: Great-circle bearing from the LL2 SLC-4E pad to the midpoint of the far edge of USCG Local Notice to Mariners 58668 Hazard Area A (SpaceX NROL-136 launch operations). Far-edge vertices 30.9500N 118.6833W (447.3 km, bearing 155.72 deg) and 31.0167N 118.6167W (443.1 km, bearing 154.58 deg). Midpoint 30.9833N 118.6500W, bearing 155.15 deg, 445.2 km. Primary window on that notice is 21 Nov 1230-1325Z, matching the LL2 open. Area B of the same notice and NOTAM MMFR B4576/26 are the further stage-1 boxes and were not used to set the azimuth. Non-rotating inclination from this pad and 155.15 deg is 69.77 deg.

payload_kg.assumption: Fixed, not fitted. The shared Falcon 9 fit bounds start at 13.0 t (a 27-satellite Starlink V2 mini band). At 13 t, after this flight's RTLS MECO at T+131 s, steering cannot reach the assumed 310 x 425 km orbit (SMA about 161 km low, geodetic altitude 182 km). 8000 kg is a round mass inside an unpublished Starshield batch at which the fitted steering does reach that assumed orbit. It is NOT an estimate of the NROL-136 payload.

insertion_alt_km.assumption: NROL-136 elements are unpublished. 310 km perigee is borrowed from the early orbit reported for the first proliferated-architecture batch, NROL-146: Langbroek, launch-night shadow entry near 300 km and a cautious elset of 310 x 311 km at 69.72 deg (https://sattrackcam.blogspot.com/2024/05/the-nrol-146-payloads-observing-train.html). Wikipedia's proliferated-architecture table lists 425 x 310 km at 69.7 deg for NROL-146, NROL-149, NROL-153 and NROL-57 (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NRO_Proliferated_Architecture_Mission). Those are not this flight's elements.

apoapsis_alt_km.assumption: Apogee borrowed from the same Wikipedia table (425 x 310 km) for prior proliferated batches. Not an NROL-136 source. The 155.15 deg hazard azimuth is not retuned toward 69.7 deg; the non-rotating inclination from the azimuth is already 69.77 deg.

target.altitude_reference: equatorial-radius (r - 6378.137 km) for SMA; insertion altitude residual uses geodetic altitude
